name: Methuselah
summary: Son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah. At 969 years he is the longest-lived person in the Bible.
catholic: Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:37). His proverbial age illustrates the long lifespans of the generations before the Flood, which Genesis shows shrinking as sin spreads.
know: Lived 969 years, the longest recorded life (Gen 5:27)
Son of Enoch, father of Lamech, grandfather of Noah
Not the same as Methushael of Cain's line

name: Pharaoh's daughter
summary: Daughter of the Pharaoh who ordered the Hebrew boys drowned. She found the infant Moses in a basket among the reeds, had compassion on him, hired his own mother as nurse, and raised him as her son, giving him his name.
catholic: Pharaoh's daughter shows mercy that defies her father's death-decree, and God uses a Gentile woman's compassion to preserve Israel's deliverer. Stephen recalls her in his speech (Acts 7:21), and Hebrews 11:24 notes that Moses by faith refused to be called her son.
know: Found Moses in the Nile (Exo 2:5-6).
Named him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water' (Exo 2:10).
Unnamed in Exodus.

name: Sons of Korah
summary: The Levite descendants of Korah, who survived their ancestor's rebellion and served as Temple gatekeepers and singers. Eleven psalms bear their name (Ps 42-49 and 84, 85, 87, 88), among them 'As the deer pants for the water brooks' and 'How lovely are your dwellings'.
catholic: The Korahite psalms are beloved in Catholic liturgy: Psalm 43 (42 in the Vulgate, a continuation of the Korahite Psalm 42) opened the traditional prayers at the foot of the altar ('I will go to the altar of God'), and Psalm 84 expresses longing for God's house. That the sons of a rebel became singers of praise is a sign of God's mercy across generations.
know: Group entry.
Survived Korah's rebellion (Num 26:11).
Gatekeepers of the tent (1 Chr 9:19).
Psalms 42-49, 84-85, 87-88 bear their name.
Heman the singer was of this family.

name: Stephen
summary: Stephen, 'a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit', was first among the Seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church. He worked great signs and debated with members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen, who brought him before the council on charges of blasphemy against the Temple and the Law. After a long speech retelling Israel's history, he saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand; he was stoned outside the city while praying for his killers, with young Saul approving.
catholic: St Stephen is the Protomartyr, the first to give his life for Christ; his feast on December 26, the day after Christmas, joins the birth of Christ to the 'birth into heaven' of his first witness. His death closely echoes Christ's Passion: he commends his spirit to the Lord Jesus and forgives his persecutors (Acts 7:59-60). The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571). The Fathers (e.g. St Augustine) saw Paul's conversion as fruit of Stephen's prayer. His relics were discovered in 415 and spread his cult widely.
know: One of the Seven chosen in Acts 6 and the first named.
Gave the longest speech in Acts (Acts 7).
Saw 'the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God' (Acts 7:56).
First Christian martyr; feast December 26.
His death began a persecution that scattered the Church beyond Jerusalem (Acts 8:1-4, 11:19).

name: Tamar
summary: Wife of Judah's son Er and then, by levirate duty, of Onan; both died. When Judah failed to give her his son Shelah, she disguised herself and conceived by Judah himself, keeping his seal, cord and staff as proof. Judah confessed 'She is more righteous than I,' and she bore the twins Perez and Zerah.
catholic: Tamar is the first of four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:3), with Rahab, Ruth and 'the wife of Uriah'; Church Fathers such as St John Chrysostom saw in them a sign that Christ came to save sinners and Gentiles and was not ashamed of his ancestry. Her determination secured the line of Judah through which David and the Messiah came.
know: Widow of Er and Onan (Gen 38:6-10)
Kept Judah's signet, cord and staff (Gen 38:18)
'She is more righteous than I' (Gen 38:26)
Mother of the twins Perez and Zerah
Named in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:3)

name: Zebulun
summary: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, whose name Leah linked to her hope that Jacob would 'honour' (dwell with) her. Jacob foretold he would dwell at the shore of the sea.
catholic: With Naphtali, his land is the 'Galilee of the nations' where Isaiah's great light dawns, fulfilled in Jesus' ministry (Isa 9:1-2; Mt 4:13-16).
know: Son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 30:19-20)
Father of Sered, Elon and Jahleel (Gen 46:14)
'Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea' (Gen 49:13)

name: Aquila
summary: Aquila, a Jew from Pontus, came to Corinth with his wife Priscilla after Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome. Paul stayed and worked with them as a fellow tentmaker; they travelled with him to Ephesus, where they took Apollos aside and explained the way of God more accurately.
catholic: Priscilla and Aquila are the New Testament's great missionary couple: tentmakers who worked with Paul, risked their lives for him, hosted a church in their home, and taught the faith. They show marriage as a partnership in the apostolate and the home as a 'domestic church' (cf. CCC 1655-1657). They are commemorated together in the Roman Martyrology (July 8).
know: A Jew of Pontus and a tentmaker.
Always named with his wife Priscilla (Prisca).
Instructed Apollos at Ephesus (Acts 18:26).
Hosted a church in their house (1 Cor 16:19; Rom 16:5).

name: Delilah
summary: Woman of the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. Bribed by the Philistine lords with eleven hundred pieces of silver each, she pressed him until he revealed that his strength lay in his uncut hair, then had it shaved while he slept and handed him to the Philistines.
catholic: Delilah's betrayal of Samson for silver has been compared by Christian writers to Judas' betrayal of Christ. Her persistent pressure is also a classic image of temptation that wears down resistance.
know: From the valley of Sorek (Jdg 16:4).
Paid by the Philistine lords (Jdg 16:5).
Had Samson's hair cut (Jdg 16:19).

name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
summary: Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian eunuch in Zedekiah's palace, pleaded with the king when Jeremiah was left to die in a muddy cistern, then drew him out with ropes and padded rags. Jeremiah gave him God's promise that he would be spared when the city fell, 'because you have put your trust in me'.
catholic: A Gentile who shows mercy to God's prophet when Israel's own leaders do not, Ebed-melech is often read alongside the Ethiopian eunuch of Acts 8 as a sign that salvation is offered to all nations through faith.
know: His name means 'servant of the king'.
Rescued Jeremiah from the cistern with thirty men (Jer 38:7-13).
Promised deliverance because he trusted in the Lord (Jer 39:15-18).

name: Eliphaz the Temanite
summary: The first and senior of Job's three friends, from Teman in Edom. He argued that the innocent never perish and that Job must have sinned, appealing to a mysterious night vision. God told him that he and his friends had not spoken rightly of him, and they were forgiven only through Job's prayer.
catholic: The friends illustrate a too-simple theology of retribution that the book corrects; their pardon through Job's intercession and sacrifice (Job 42:8-9) has been read as a figure of Christ's priestly intercession.
know: Speaks in Job 4-5, 15, 22.
Rebuked by God (Job 42:7).
Not to be confused with Esau's son Eliphaz.

name: Herod Agrippa I
summary: Herod Agrippa I, grandson of Herod the Great, is called simply 'Herod the king' in Acts 12. To please the Jewish leaders he had James the brother of John killed with the sword and imprisoned Peter, who was freed by an angel. At Caesarea, when the crowd hailed his speech as 'the voice of a god', an angel of the Lord struck him because he did not give God the glory, and he died eaten by worms.
catholic: He is the first ruler to make an apostle a martyr (St James, Acts 12:2). The Church's unceasing prayer for the imprisoned Peter (Acts 12:5) is a classic image of the Church praying for the Pope. His death illustrates the downfall of pride that claims divine honor.
know: Called 'Herod' in Acts 12; identified by the historian Josephus as Agrippa I.
Executed James son of Zebedee and imprisoned Peter.
Struck down by an angel at Caesarea (Acts 12:23).
According to Josephus, father of Agrippa II, Bernice and Drusilla.

name: Herodias
summary: Herodias, granddaughter of Herod the Great, left her husband Philip to marry his brother Herod Antipas. When John the Baptist declared the marriage unlawful, she nursed a grudge against him, and at Herod's birthday feast she prompted her daughter to ask for John's head on a platter.
catholic: Herodias is often compared with Jezebel, who persecuted Elijah, since Jesus identifies John with Elijah. John's death for rebuking her marriage makes him a martyr for the indissolubility and holiness of marriage.
know: Wife first of Philip, then of his brother Herod Antipas (Mk 6:17).
Held a grudge against John the Baptist (Mk 6:19).
Prompted her daughter to request John's head (Mt 14:8).

name: Ittai the Gittite
summary: Ittai, a Philistine of Gath newly come to David with six hundred men, refused to turn back when David fled Absalom: 'wherever my lord the king is, in death or in life, there your servant will be'. He commanded a third of David's army.
catholic: Ittai, a foreigner, pledges loyalty to the rejected king in words close to Ruth's and to Peter's 'Lord, I will go with you to death' - an image of Gentiles cleaving to the rejected Messiah.
know: A Philistine from Gath
Swore loyalty to David in exile
Commanded a third of the army

name: Jael
summary: Wife of Heber the Kenite, who welcomed the fleeing Sisera into her tent, gave him milk, covered him, and while he slept drove a tent peg through his temple, fulfilling Deborah's word that the LORD would sell Sisera into a woman's hand.
catholic: The Song of Deborah calls Jael 'blessed above women' (Jdg 5:24), words echoed of Judith (Jdt 13:18) and of Mary by Elizabeth (Lk 1:42). Patristic and medieval writers read her, like Judith, as a type of Mary, through whom the enemy's head is crushed (cf. Gen 3:15).
know: Wife of Heber the Kenite (Jdg 4:17).
Killed Sisera with a tent peg (Jdg 4:21).
'Blessed above women' (Jdg 5:24).

name: Obadiah
summary: Obadiah, who 'feared the LORD greatly', was in charge of Ahab's household; when Jezebel was killing the prophets he hid a hundred of them in two caves and fed them. He arranged Elijah's meeting with Ahab before Carmel.
catholic: Some Jewish tradition identified him with the prophet Obadiah, but Scripture does not. He is a model of the believer who serves faithfully and courageously within a hostile court.
know: Hid 100 prophets in caves
Brought Ahab to meet Elijah

name: Onan
summary: Judah's second son, told to raise offspring for his dead brother Er by Tamar (the levirate duty). Knowing the child would not count as his, he spilled his seed on the ground, and the LORD put him to death.
catholic: Catholic moral tradition has cited Onan's act in teaching on the integrity of the marital act; Pius XI's encyclical Casti Connubii (1930), quoting St Augustine, refers to it. The text also stresses his refusal of the duty to his dead brother.
know: Second son of Judah (Gen 38:4)
Refused to raise offspring for Er (Gen 38:9)
The LORD put him to death (Gen 38:10)

name: Othniel
summary: Son of Kenaz, of Caleb's family, who captured Kiriath Sepher (Debir) and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as wife. When Israel served Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia for eight years, the Spirit of the LORD came upon him; he delivered Israel and the land had rest forty years. He is the first of the judges.
catholic: Othniel is the model judge in whom the pattern of the book is laid out plainly: sin, oppression, crying out, a Spirit-filled deliverer, and rest. The Church reads the judges' Spirit-given deliverance as a foreshadowing of Christ, on whom the Spirit rests fully (Isa 11:2; Lk 4:18).
know: First judge of Israel (Jdg 3:9).
Took Kiriath Sepher and married Achsah (Jos 15:17).
Defeated Cushan Rishathaim (Jdg 3:10).
The land had rest forty years (Jdg 3:11).

name: Priscilla
summary: Priscilla (Prisca) was the wife of Aquila and, with him, a co-worker of Paul at Corinth, Ephesus and Rome. Paul thanks them for risking their necks for his life, and the churches of the Gentiles give thanks for them.
catholic: Priscilla and Aquila are the New Testament's great missionary couple: tentmakers who worked with Paul, risked their lives for him, hosted a church in their home, and taught the faith. They show marriage as a partnership in the apostolate and the home as a 'domestic church' (cf. CCC 1655-1657). They are commemorated together in the Roman Martyrology (July 8). That she is often named before her husband suggests her prominence in the community.
know: Called Prisca by Paul.
Explained the way of God to Apollos with Aquila (Acts 18:26).
Paul's 'fellow worker in Christ Jesus' (Rom 16:3).

name: Zechariah
summary: Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, began to prophesy in 520 BC alongside Haggai, encouraging the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple. His night visions include the high priest Joshua clothed in clean garments, the golden lampstand and the two olive trees ('not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit'), and his later oracles speak of a humble king riding on a donkey, a shepherd valued at thirty pieces of silver, and one 'whom they have pierced'.
catholic: The Gospels read Zechariah's oracles as fulfilled in the Passion: Jesus enters Jerusalem on Palm Sunday as the king 'humble, and riding on a donkey' (Zech 9:9; Mt 21:4-5; Jn 12:15; CCC 559); he is betrayed for thirty pieces of silver (Zech 11:12-13; Mt 27:9); the shepherd is struck and the sheep scattered (Zech 13:7; Mt 26:31); and they look on him whom they have pierced (Zech 12:10; Jn 19:37), a text the Church contemplates in devotion to the pierced Heart of Jesus. The crowning of Joshua (Jeshua) as 'the Branch' (Zech 6:11-13) was read by the Fathers as a figure of Christ, priest and king — whose Hebrew name is the same as Joshua's.
know: Son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo (Zech 1:1); Ezra calls him 'son of Iddo'.
Eight night visions (Zech 1-6).
King riding on a donkey (Zech 9:9) — Palm Sunday.
'They will look on me whom they have pierced' (Zech 12:10).

name: Achiacharus (Ahikar)
summary: Tobit's nephew, son of his brother Anael, who rose to be cupbearer, keeper of the signet and chief administrator under the Assyrian king Esarhaddon ('Sarchedonus'). He interceded to bring Tobit back to Nineveh and supported him during his blindness. He is the hero of the ancient Near Eastern 'Story of Ahikar', in which his adopted nephew betrays him.
catholic: Tobit appeals to Ahikar's story as proof that almsgiving delivers from death while treachery falls into its own snare (Tob 14:10-11). The cameo shows the inspired author drawing on wider wisdom traditions.
know: Known outside the Bible as Ahikar.
Cupbearer and keeper of the signet under Sarchedonus (Esarhaddon).
Supported blind Tobit (Tob 2:10).
Attended Tobias' wedding feast with Nasbas (Tob 11:18).

name: Achsah
summary: Daughter of Caleb, promised to whoever captured Kiriath Sepher and given to Othniel. She urged her husband to ask for a field and herself asked her father for springs of water, receiving the upper and lower springs.
catholic: Achsah's bold, successful petition to her father has been used by spiritual writers as an image of confident prayer to God the Father.
know: Daughter of Caleb (Jos 15:16).
Wife of Othniel.
Asked for and received springs of water (Jos 15:18-19).

name: Ananias of Damascus
summary: Ananias was a devout disciple in Damascus. In a vision the Lord sent him to Saul, who had been blinded on the road; despite his fear of the persecutor, he went, laid his hands on him, and Saul regained his sight and was baptized.
catholic: Ananias is honored as the man who welcomed the Church's fiercest enemy as 'Brother Saul' and baptized him (Acts 9:17-18; 22:16). The Lord's words to him, that Saul is 'my chosen vessel', express the Church's understanding of Paul's vocation.
know: Sent by the Lord in a vision to the house of Judah on Straight Street (Acts 9:10-11).
Called Saul 'Brother' and laid hands on him.
Baptized Saul (Acts 9:18; 22:16).
Paul describes him as devout and respected by the Jews (Acts 22:12).

name: Ethan the Ezrahite
summary: A Merarite Levite musician appointed under David with Heman and Asaph, and one of the wise men whom Solomon surpassed. Psalm 89, on God's covenant with David and its apparent failure, is ascribed to him.
catholic: Psalm 89 ('I have made a covenant with my chosen one', Ps 89:3) is a central text for the Church's reading of Christ as the eternal Son of David; it is sung at Christmas Vigil and on the solemnity of St Joseph.
know: Son of Kishi/Kushaiah, of Merari (1 Chr 6:44; 15:17).
Psalm 89 bears his name.
Named in 1 Kgs 4:31.
Possibly identical with Jeduthun.

name: Eve
summary: The first woman, built by God from the man's rib to be his partner. Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and gave it to Adam; God announced enmity between the serpent and the woman's offspring. Adam named her Eve because she was 'the mother of all the living'; she bore Cain, Abel and Seth.
catholic: The Fathers contrast Eve with Mary, the New Eve: St Irenaeus wrote that 'the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience', and St Jerome 'death through Eve, life through Mary' (both quoted in CCC 494). Gen 3:15, the 'protoevangelium' or first announcement of the Gospel, is read by Christian tradition as foretelling the New Adam and the New Eve, Mary, who shares in his victory over sin (CCC 410-411). Mary is thus honoured as the true 'mother of the living' in the order of grace. The Catechism also names Eve among the women whose mission prepared for Mary's (CCC 489).
know: Created from Adam's rib as 'bone of my bones' (Gen 2:21-23)
Name means roughly 'living': 'mother of all the living' (Gen 3:20)
Gen 3:15 promises enmity between the woman's offspring and the serpent
The Fathers call Mary the 'New Eve'
Mother of Cain, Abel and Seth (Gen 4:1-2, 25)

name: Joses
summary: Joses is named among the 'brothers' of Jesus at Nazareth (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3) and as a son of the Mary who watched the crucifixion and burial (Mt 27:56; Mk 15:40, 47).
catholic: Joses shows the Catholic reading of the 'brothers of the Lord': he and James are explicitly sons of another Mary, so they are Jesus' kinsmen rather than children of the Virgin Mary (CCC 500).
know: Brother of James 'the less' (Mk 15:40).
His mother 'Mary the mother of Joses' saw where Jesus was laid (Mk 15:47).
Not to be confused with Joses called Barnabas (Acts 4:36).

name: Michael
summary: Michael is 'one of the chief princes' who helps the angel speaking to Daniel against the prince of Persia, and 'the great prince who stands for the children of your people' at the end time. In the New Testament he disputes with the devil over Moses' body and leads the angels in the war in heaven against the dragon.
catholic: St Michael is venerated as protector of the Church and defender against Satan; the Prayer to St Michael composed under Pope Leo XIII ('defend us in battle') is widely prayed. The Church celebrates him with Sts Gabriel and Raphael on September 29 and remembers him in the liturgy (CCC 335).
know: Name means 'Who is like God?'
Protector of God's people (Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1).
Called 'the archangel' in Jude 9.
Casts down the dragon in Revelation 12:7-9.

name: Nathan son of David
summary: Nathan, a son of David and Bathsheba born in Jerusalem, is otherwise unknown in the Old Testament, but Luke traces the genealogy of Jesus back to David through him rather than through Solomon.
catholic: Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:31) runs through Nathan, Matthew's through Solomon. A long tradition, found already in early writers, explains the two lines as Mary's (Luke) and Joseph's (Matthew), or as Joseph's natural and legal descent; either way both make Jesus truly 'Son of David'. Zechariah 12:12 mentions 'the family of the house of Nathan' mourning the pierced one.
know: Son of Bathsheba, full brother of Solomon
Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
Not the prophet Nathan

name: Nicodemus
role: Pharisee; ruler of the Jews; disciple
summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin, came to Jesus by night and was taught that one must be born of water and the Spirit to enter the Kingdom of God. Later he urged the council to give Jesus a fair hearing, and after the crucifixion he brought about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes to help Joseph of Arimathea bury Jesus.
catholic: Jesus' words to Nicodemus, 'unless one is born of water and the Spirit' (Jn 3:5), are a foundational text for the necessity of Baptism (CCC 1215, 1257), and the same discourse contains 'God so loved the world' (Jn 3:16). He is cited with Joseph of Arimathea as one of the religious leaders who were secret disciples (CCC 595). His journey from night to open devotion models gradual conversion.
know: Came to Jesus by night (Jn 3:2).
Heard 'born of water and the Spirit' and 'God so loved the world' (Jn 3:5, 16).
Defended Jesus before the Pharisees (Jn 7:50-51).
Helped bury Jesus with myrrh and aloes (Jn 19:39).
feast: August 31 (Sts Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, Roman Martyrology)

name: Oholiab
summary: Son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, appointed by God to assist Bezalel. He was an engraver, designer and embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet, and teacher of others in the work of the tabernacle.
catholic: With Bezalel, Oholiab shows that craftsmanship and beauty serve the worship of God; the pairing of a man of Judah and a man of Dan has been noted as all Israel contributing to the sanctuary.
know: Son of Ahisamach, of Dan (Exo 31:6).
Engraver, designer and embroiderer (Exo 38:23).
Given ability to teach (Exo 35:34).

name: Salmon
summary: Son of Nahshon of Judah and father of Boaz. Matthew's genealogy names Rahab of Jericho as the mother of Boaz, making Salmon her husband.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. His marriage to Rahab (Mt 1:5) brings a Canaanite woman of faith into the Messiah's ancestry.
know: Son of Nahshon (Ruth 4:20).
Father of Boaz by Rahab (Mt 1:5).
Called Salma in 1 Chr 2:11.

name: Annas
summary: Annas had been high priest (AD 6-15) and remained the senior power in the priestly family; five of his sons and his son-in-law Caiaphas held the office after him. After his arrest Jesus was led first to Annas, who questioned him about his disciples and teaching before sending him bound to Caiaphas.
catholic: Luke's phrase 'the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas' (Lk 3:2) reflects Annas's continuing authority. With Caiaphas he later confronted the apostles in Acts 4.
know: Father-in-law of Caiaphas (Jn 18:13).
Questioned Jesus first after his arrest (Jn 18:19-24).
Named with Caiaphas in Luke 3:2 and Acts 4:6.

name: Gabriel
summary: Gabriel is the angel who explains Daniel's vision of the ram and the goat and later brings him the prophecy of the seventy weeks. In the New Testament he announces the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah and the conception of Jesus to the Virgin Mary.
catholic: St Gabriel is venerated as the archangel of the Annunciation; his greeting 'Hail, full of grace' (Lk 1:28) begins the Hail Mary and the Angelus. The Church celebrates him with Sts Michael and Raphael on September 29 and remembers these angels in the liturgy (CCC 335). Daniel's seventy weeks, which Gabriel brings 'to anoint the most holy', were read by the Fathers as pointing to the time of the Messiah.
know: Name means 'God is my strength' (traditional).
Appears to Daniel twice (Dan 8:16; 9:21).
'I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God' (Lk 1:19).
Announced the Incarnation to Mary (Lk 1:26-38).

name: Hoglah
summary: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

name: Jotham (son of Gideon)
summary: Youngest son of Gideon, the only one to escape Abimelech's massacre. From Mount Gerizim he told the people of Shechem the fable of the trees who sought a king and ended with the bramble, cursing Shechem and Abimelech; then he fled to Beer.
catholic: Jotham's fable (Jdg 9:7-15), the oldest fable in Scripture, is a classic critique of power seized by the unworthy; the curse he pronounced is said to have come upon both Abimelech and Shechem (Jdg 9:57).
know: Youngest son of Gideon; hid and survived (Jdg 9:5).
Told the fable of the trees from Gerizim (Jdg 9:7-15).
His curse was fulfilled (Jdg 9:57).

name: Lamech (son of Methushael)
summary: A descendant of Cain who took two wives, Adah and Zillah, and boasted to them in a song of vengeance that he had killed a man for wounding him, claiming to be avenged 'seventy-seven times'.
catholic: Lamech's song shows sin escalating after the Fall: vengeance multiplied seventy-seven times. Many commentators note that Jesus reverses it when he tells Peter to forgive 'seventy times seven' (Mt 18:22).
know: First man recorded with two wives (Gen 4:19)
Boasted of being avenged seventy-seven times (Gen 4:24)
Not the same as Lamech father of Noah

name: Lazarus (the beggar in the parable)
summary: In Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus, a poor man covered with sores lay at a rich man's gate; at death he was carried by angels to Abraham's bosom while the rich man suffered torment. Abraham told the rich man that those who will not hear Moses and the prophets would not be persuaded even if someone rose from the dead.
catholic: Lazarus is the only named character in any of Jesus' parables. The Church cites the parable for the 'bosom of Abraham' where the just awaited Christ (CCC 633), for the immediate judgment after death, and as a summons to recognize Christ in the poor (CCC 2463).
know: The only named character in a parable of Jesus.
Carried to 'Abraham's bosom' (Lk 16:22).
Distinct from Lazarus of Bethany.

name: Mahlah
summary: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

name: Milcah
summary: Milcah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

name: Nimrod
summary: A son of Cush who 'began to be a mighty one in the earth' and 'a mighty hunter before the LORD'. His kingdom began in Babel, Erech, Accad and Calneh in Shinar, and he built Nineveh in Assyria.
catholic: Later Jewish and Christian tradition linked Nimrod with the building of the tower of Babel, but Genesis itself does not say this.
know: 'A mighty hunter before the LORD' (Gen 10:9)
His kingdom began in Babel in Shinar (Gen 10:10)
Assyria is called 'the land of Nimrod' (Mic 5:6)

name: Noah
summary: Noah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

name: Rizpah
summary: Rizpah daughter of Aiah was Saul's concubine. When her two sons were executed by the Gibeonites, she kept vigil over their bodies on a rock from the beginning of harvest until the rains, guarding them from birds and beasts; her devotion moved David to give Saul's house honourable burial.
catholic: Rizpah's long vigil over her dead sons is often seen as an icon of a mother's sorrowing fidelity, recalling the Mother standing at the Cross.
know: Abner was accused over her
Mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth
Guarded her sons' bodies for months

name: Salome
role: Disciple; mother of James and John
summary: Salome was among the women who followed Jesus from Galilee, watched the crucifixion, and came with spices to anoint his body on Easter morning (Mk 15:40; 16:1). Comparing Mark with Matthew's 'mother of the sons of Zebedee' (Mt 27:56), she is generally identified as the mother of James and John, who asked Jesus that her sons sit at his right and left in his Kingdom.
catholic: Her request prompted Jesus' teaching that greatness in the Kingdom means service and drinking his cup (Mt 20:20-28). Some interpreters also identify her with the sister of Jesus' mother at the cross (Jn 19:25), which would make James and John kinsmen of Jesus; this is uncertain. She is honoured among the myrrh-bearing women, first witnesses of the empty tomb.
know: Named only in Mark (Mk 15:40; 16:1).
Generally identified with 'the mother of the sons of Zebedee' (Mt 20:20; 27:56).
Brought spices to the tomb on Easter morning.

name: Simon Magus
summary: Simon practised sorcery in Samaria and was hailed as 'the great power of God'. He believed Philip's preaching and was baptized, but when he saw the Spirit given through the apostles' laying on of hands he offered them money for that power. Peter sharply rebuked him and called him to repent.
catholic: His attempt to buy spiritual power gave its name to the sin of simony, the buying or selling of spiritual things (CCC 2121). The episode also shows the gift of the Spirit through the apostles' laying on of hands after Baptism (Acts 8:17-18), read by the Church as a witness to Confirmation. Later legend (not Scripture) makes him the father of Gnostic heresy and an opponent of Peter at Rome.
know: Called 'the great power of God' by the Samaritans.
Baptized by Philip.
Offered money for the power to give the Spirit: origin of the word 'simony'.
Peter told him: 'May your silver perish with you' (Acts 8:20).

name: Simon the Zealot
summary: Simon, called 'the Zealot', appears in each list of the Twelve (Mt 10:4; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15; Acts 1:13), distinguished from Simon Peter by his surname.
catholic: His surname may point to zeal for the Law or to the nationalist movement; either way, Jesus gathered into one band a former 'zealot' and a former tax collector (Matthew). Tradition holds he preached with Jude in Persia, where both were martyred, so they share a feast.
know: Called 'the Zealot' to distinguish him from Peter.
Nothing else is recorded of him in Scripture.
Feast October 28, with St Jude.

name: Tirzah
summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

name: Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander the Macedonian, son of Philip, who conquered the Persian Empire of Darius III and ruled 'to the ends of the earth' for twelve years, then died and left his empire divided among his generals. 1 Maccabees opens with him to explain the origin of the Seleucid kingdom.
catholic: The Fathers identified Alexander with the swift he-goat and the 'mighty king' of Daniel's visions (Dan 8:5-8, 21; 11:3-4). His conquests spread the Greek language that became the vehicle of the Septuagint and of the New Testament — a providential preparation for the Gospel.
know: Son of Philip of Macedon (1 Macc 1:1).
Reigned twelve years (1 Macc 1:7).
Divided his kingdom among his servants (1 Macc 1:6-9).
Identified with the he-goat of Daniel 8.

name: Ananias
summary: Ananias sold a property and, with his wife Sapphira's knowledge, kept back part of the price while presenting the rest to the apostles as if it were the whole. Peter told him he had lied not to men but to the Holy Spirit, and he fell down dead.
catholic: The Fathers read the episode as a warning against hypocrisy and sacrilege in the young Church. Peter's words ('you have lied to the Holy Spirit... You haven't lied to men, but to God', Acts 5:3-4) are a classic scriptural witness that the Holy Spirit is God. It also shows Peter exercising authority and discernment over the community.
know: Kept back part of the price of a field while pretending to give all.
Peter said he had lied to the Holy Spirit, i.e. to God.
Fell dead at Peter's word; his wife Sapphira died three hours later.

name: Asenath
summary: Egyptian daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, given to Joseph as wife by Pharaoh; she bore Manasseh and Ephraim before the years of famine.
catholic: Asenath, an Egyptian woman whose sons became two tribes of Israel, is often noted as one of the Gentile women grafted into God's people. The later Jewish romance 'Joseph and Aseneth' tells of her conversion, but it is not Scripture.
know: Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On (Gen 41:45)
Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (Gen 41:50-52)
Her sons became heads of two tribes

name: Demas
summary: Demas is listed as Paul's fellow worker in Colossians and Philemon, but in 2 Timothy Paul laments that 'Demas left me, having loved this present world'.
catholic: Demas is a sobering example of perseverance lost: the love of 'this present world' drawing a disciple away from the mission.
know: A fellow worker of Paul (Philem 24).
Deserted Paul for Thessalonica (2 Tim 4:10).

name: Epaphras
role: Founder of the church at Colossae
summary: Epaphras, a Colossian, taught the Colossians the gospel and laboured for the churches of Laodicea and Hierapolis. He was with Paul as a 'fellow prisoner', always wrestling in prayer for his people.
catholic: He is a model of the pastor who intercedes constantly for his flock (Col 4:12-13).
know: The Colossians learned the gospel from him (Col 1:7).
Paul's fellow prisoner (Philem 23).
Prayed earnestly for Colossae, Laodicea and Hierapolis (Col 4:12-13).

name: Ezekiel
summary: Ezekiel son of Buzi, a priest, was deported to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC and was called by the river Chebar in a vision of God's glory on a chariot of living creatures. He announced Jerusalem's fall through dramatic sign-acts, saw God's glory leave the Temple, and after 587 BC proclaimed restoration: a new heart and spirit, the valley of dry bones, the good shepherd and a new Temple from which life-giving water flows.
catholic: The Church reads Ezek 36:25-27 (clean water, a new heart, God's Spirit within) as a prophecy of Baptism and the gift of the Spirit (cf. Jn 3:5; CCC 1287), and it is the seventh Old Testament reading of the Easter Vigil; the Easter-season sprinkling antiphon 'Vidi aquam' draws on the water flowing from the Temple (Ezek 47). The dry bones (Ezek 37) prefigure the resurrection, and God's promise to shepherd his flock himself (Ezek 34) is fulfilled in Christ the Good Shepherd (Jn 10). Fathers such as St Ambrose and St Jerome read the shut eastern gate through which only the Lord enters (Ezek 44:2) as a figure of Mary's perpetual virginity, and the four faces of the living creatures (Ezek 1:10) became the symbols of the four Evangelists.
know: A priest in exile, called 'son of man' by God over ninety times.
Ate the scroll of God's word (Ezek 2:8-3:3) and was made Israel's watchman (Ezek 3:17).
His wife's death became a sign he was forbidden to mourn (Ezek 24:15-24).
Visions: God's glory, the dry bones, the new Temple and its river (Ezek 1; 37; 47).

name: Hosea
summary: Hosea son of Beeri prophesied in the northern kingdom in the last decades before its fall (8th century BC). God commanded him to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, and to give their children names of judgment — Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi — so that his broken marriage became a living parable of Israel's infidelity and of God's unfailing, redeeming love.
catholic: Hosea is the great prophet of God's spousal love: the Church teaches that the prophets, seeing God's covenant with Israel in the image of exclusive and faithful married love, prepared the way for the New Covenant in which Christ is Bridegroom of the Church (CCC 1611; Eph 5:25-32). 'Out of Egypt I called my son' (Hos 11:1) is fulfilled in the Holy Family's return (Mt 2:15); Jesus twice quotes 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' (Hos 6:6; Mt 9:13; 12:7); and 'on the third day he will raise us up' (Hos 6:2) was read by the Fathers in light of the Resurrection. Paul and Peter apply 'Not my people... my people' to the Church gathered from Jews and Gentiles (Rom 9:25-26; 1 Pet 2:10).
know: Son of Beeri, prophet to the northern kingdom under Jeroboam II.
Married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim (Hos 1:3).
His children's names were prophecies: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah ('not pitied'), Lo-ammi ('not my people').
'I will allure her... into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her' (Hos 2:14).
First of the Twelve (Minor) Prophets in canonical order.

name: Hur
summary: Leader of Israel who, with Aaron, went up the hill with Moses during the battle against Amalek and held up Moses' hands until sunset, so Israel prevailed. When Moses ascended Sinai he left Aaron and Hur in charge of the people.
catholic: The image of Aaron and Hur supporting the arms of Moses at prayer (Exo 17:12) has been used by the Fathers as a figure of the outstretched arms of Christ on the Cross, and more widely of the support the faithful give to the prayer of their shepherds.
know: Held up Moses' hands with Aaron at Rephidim (Exo 17:10-12).
Left in charge with Aaron while Moses was on Sinai (Exo 24:14).
Jewish tradition identifies him with the grandfather of Bezalel, but Scripture does not say so.

name: Joseph son of Zacharias
summary: Left with Azarias to guard Judea while Judas and his brothers campaigned in Gilead and Galilee; seeking glory against orders, the two attacked Jamnia and were routed by Gorgias with the loss of two thousand men.
catholic: 1 Maccabees comments that 'they were not of the family of those men by whose hand deliverance was given to Israel' (1 Macc 5:62) — success depends on God's chosen instruments, not on the desire to 'get a name'.
know: Defeated by Gorgias at Jamnia (1 Macc 5:59-60).

name: Judas Barsabbas
summary: Judas called Barsabbas was one of the 'chief men among the brothers' chosen by the apostles and elders, with Silas, to carry the decision of the Council of Jerusalem to Antioch. Being a prophet, he encouraged and strengthened the brothers there.
catholic: He was one of the bearers of the apostolic letter of Acts 15, which spoke with the authority of 'the Holy Spirit and us' (Acts 15:28), an early witness to the Church's teaching authority.
know: Chosen with Silas to carry the Council's letter to Antioch.
A prophet who strengthened the church (Acts 15:32).

name: Luke
summary: Luke, 'the beloved physician', was a companion of Paul who stayed with him to the end ('Only Luke is with me'). The 'we' passages of Acts (from Acts 16:10) suggest that the author travelled with Paul to Philippi, to Jerusalem, and on the voyage to Rome.
catholic: The Church honors St Luke as the author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles; his feast is October 18 and his symbol is the ox. His Gospel gives the Church the infancy narratives and the canticles prayed daily in the Liturgy of the Hours (the Benedictus, Magnificat and Nunc Dimittis), and Acts recounts the birth of the Church at Pentecost. Tradition holds that he painted icons of the Virgin Mary; he is patron of physicians and artists.
know: Called 'the beloved physician' (Col 4:14).
Faithful to Paul in his final imprisonment (2 Tim 4:11).
Traditionally the author of Luke and Acts, both addressed to Theophilus.
Feast October 18.

name: Simon of Cyrene
summary: Simon, a man of Cyrene coming in from the country, was compelled by the soldiers to carry Jesus' cross to Golgotha. Mark names him as the father of Alexander and Rufus, evidently known to Mark's readers.
catholic: Simon is remembered in the Fifth Station of the Cross. Luke's phrase that he carried the cross 'after Jesus' (Lk 23:26) makes him an image of every disciple who takes up the cross and follows Christ (Lk 9:23).
know: From Cyrene in North Africa (Mt 27:32).
Compelled to carry Jesus' cross (Mk 15:21).
Father of Alexander and Rufus (Mk 15:21).

name: Simon the Pharisee
summary: Simon, a Pharisee, invited Jesus to dine. When a sinful woman wept at Jesus' feet, wiped them with her hair and anointed them, Simon doubted Jesus was a prophet; Jesus told the parable of the two debtors and declared, 'Her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much'.
catholic: The episode teaches the link between forgiveness and love and is a classic text for the sacrament of Penance and for contrition born of love. Western tradition after St Gregory the Great identified the sinful woman with Mary Magdalene, a view the Church no longer assumes.
know: A Pharisee who hosted Jesus (Lk 7:36, 40).
Heard the parable of the two debtors (Lk 7:41-43).
Distinct in the text from Simon the leper of Bethany.

name: Simon the tanner
summary: Simon was a tanner at Joppa whose house was by the sea. Peter stayed with him many days, and it was on his roof that Peter saw the vision of the sheet of clean and unclean animals before going to Cornelius.
catholic: A tanner's trade made him ritually unclean in the eyes of strict Jews; Peter's lodging with him quietly anticipates the vision that opens the Church to the Gentiles.
know: A tanner whose house stood by the sea at Joppa.
Peter received the vision of the sheet on his roof (Acts 10:9-16).

name: Stephanas
summary: Stephanas and his household were the first converts of Achaia and devoted themselves to serving the saints; Paul baptized them himself. He came to Paul with Fortunatus and Achaicus, and Paul asks the Corinthians to be subject to such workers.
catholic: The baptism of his household (1 Cor 1:16) is among the household baptisms cited in the Church's tradition of baptizing whole families.
know: His household was 'the first fruits of Achaia' (1 Cor 16:15).
Baptized by Paul with his household (1 Cor 1:16).
Visited Paul at Ephesus (1 Cor 16:17).

name: Tabitha
summary: Tabitha, called Dorcas in Greek (both mean 'gazelle'), was a disciple at Joppa full of good works and almsgiving, who made garments for widows. When she died, Peter was summoned; he knelt, prayed, and said 'Tabitha, get up', and she was restored to life.
catholic: She is a model of the corporal works of mercy, especially care for widows and the poor. Her raising echoes Jesus' raising of Jairus' daughter ('Talitha, koum') and shows Peter acting with Christ's own power.
know: Also called Dorcas; both names mean 'gazelle'.
Known for clothing the widows of Joppa.
Raised from the dead by Peter.

name: The Shunammite woman
summary: A wealthy woman of Shunem persuaded Elisha to eat at her house and, with her husband, built him a small upper room. Elisha promised her a son; years later the boy died in her lap, and she rode to Mount Carmel, clung to Elisha's feet and would not leave him until he came and raised the child. Warned of famine, she lived seven years in Philistia, and the king restored her land.
catholic: Her hospitality to the man of God is read on the 13th Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year A) with Jesus' words 'whoever receives a prophet...'. The raising of her son anticipates Jesus raising the widow's son at Nain, near Shunem (Lk 7:11-17), and her faith - 'It is well' - is a model of trust in grief.
know: Built a room for Elisha
Received a son by Elisha's promise
Her son was raised from the dead
Her land was restored by the king

name: Uriah son of Shemaiah
summary: Uriah of Kiriath-jearim prophesied the same message as Jeremiah. When King Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but was brought back by Elnathan and struck down with the sword.
catholic: He belongs to the line of prophets slain for God's word whom Jesus laments (Mt 23:37).
know: A faithful prophet martyred by Jehoiakim (Jer 26:20-23).
His fate shows the danger Jeremiah faced.

name: Widow of Zarephath
summary: During the drought God sent Elijah to a Gentile widow at Zarephath in Sidon who was gathering sticks to bake a last meal for herself and her son. She gave Elijah her little cake first, and her jar of flour and jug of oil did not fail until the rain came. When her son died, Elijah stretched himself on the child three times and the LORD restored his life.
catholic: Jesus cites her in his Nazareth sermon (Lk 4:25-26) - Elijah was sent to none of Israel's widows but to her - as a sign that God's mercy reaches the Gentiles; the passage is read on the Monday of the 3rd week of Lent. Her gift from her poverty is paired liturgically with the widow's mite (32nd Sunday, Year B), and the unfailing flour and oil have been read as a figure of the Eucharist. The Catechism notes that Elijah taught her to believe in God's word (CCC 2583).
know: A Gentile widow in Sidon
Fed Elijah with her last flour and oil
Her flour and oil did not run out
Her son was raised by Elijah
Mentioned by Jesus in Luke 4

name: Zacchaeus
summary: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector of Jericho, was short and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Jesus called him down and stayed at his house; Zacchaeus promised half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution to any he had defrauded, and Jesus declared, 'Today, salvation has come to this house'.
catholic: Zacchaeus is the Church's model of conversion shown in restitution: the Catechism cites his pledge in teaching that justice requires restoring what was unjustly taken (CCC 2412). His story is the Gospel for the Dedication of a Church, as Christ comes to dwell in his house, and ends with the mission statement 'the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost'.
know: Chief tax collector at Jericho (Lk 19:2).
Climbed a sycamore to see Jesus (Lk 19:4).
Promised fourfold restitution (Lk 19:8).
'Today, salvation has come to this house' (Lk 19:9).

name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada
summary: After Jehoiada's death the princes of Judah turned to idols; Jehoiada's son Zechariah, clothed by the Spirit of God, rebuked them, and at King Joash's command he was stoned in the Temple court, crying 'May the LORD look on it and avenge it'.
catholic: Jesus speaks of the blood of the righteous 'from Abel to Zechariah', killed between the sanctuary and the altar (Mt 23:35; Lk 11:51) - a reference generally taken to this Zechariah, the last murder recorded in the last book of the Hebrew canon. Matthew calls him 'son of Barachiah', a difficulty discussed since the Fathers. He prefigures the martyrs and Christ, the prophet rejected in the Temple.
know: Spoke by the Spirit of God
Stoned in the Temple court at Joash's command
Cited by Jesus with Abel

name: Zipporah
summary: Daughter of Jethro (Reuel), priest of Midian, given to Moses as wife after he defended her and her sisters at a well. She bore him Gershom and Eliezer and, on the road back to Egypt, circumcised her son to avert the LORD's threat against Moses.
catholic: Zipporah's urgent circumcision of her son (Exo 4:24-26) underlines the seriousness of the covenant sign, which the Church sees fulfilled in Baptism, the 'circumcision of Christ' (Col 2:11-12). As a Midianite woman joined to Moses she is also read as a sign of the nations being drawn into God's people.
know: Daughter of the priest of Midian (Exo 2:16-21).
Mother of Gershom and Eliezer.
Circumcised her son with a flint (Exo 4:25).
Brought back to Moses by Jethro at Sinai (Exo 18:2-6).
Whether the 'Cushite woman' of Num 12:1 is Zipporah or a second wife is debated.

name: Adoni-Zedek
summary: Amorite king of Jerusalem who, alarmed at Gibeon's treaty with Israel, formed a coalition of five kings to attack Gibeon. Joshua routed them in the battle when the sun stood still; the kings hid in a cave at Makkedah and were executed.
catholic: His name ('my lord is righteousness') echoes that of Melchizedek, earlier king of Salem; Christian writers have contrasted the unjust king of Jerusalem with Christ, the true King of Righteousness.
know: King of Jerusalem (Jos 10:1).
Led the five-king coalition against Gibeon.
Executed at Makkedah (Jos 10:22-27).

name: Aeneas
summary: Aeneas of Lydda had been bedridden and paralysed for eight years. Peter said to him, 'Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed', and he rose at once; many in Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord.
catholic: His healing, in the name of Jesus Christ, shows the apostles continuing Christ's works of healing, a sign the Church sees fulfilled in the sacraments of healing.
know: Paralysed for eight years.
Healed by Peter at Lydda in Jesus' name.

name: Agabus
summary: Agabus was a prophet from Jerusalem who foretold by the Spirit a great famine in the days of Claudius, prompting the Antioch church to send relief to Judea. Years later at Caesarea he bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to foretell Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.
catholic: Agabus witnesses to the charism of prophecy in the apostolic Church. His first prophecy led to the first recorded collection between churches (Acts 11:29-30), an early sign of communion and charity among local Churches.
know: Predicted a worldwide famine under Claudius (Acts 11:28).
Acted out Paul's coming arrest with Paul's belt (Acts 21:10-11).

name: Asmodaeus
summary: 'The evil spirit' who killed each of Sarah's seven husbands on their wedding night. When Tobias burned the fish's heart and liver as Raphael instructed, the demon fled to upper Egypt, where Raphael bound him.
catholic: The episode illustrates the Church's teaching that the devil and demons are real but defeated creatures whose power is limited by God (CCC 391-395). The remedy combines a sign with prayer — the couple rise and pray together (Tob 8:4-8) — and Christian tradition has seen in it a figure of deliverance from evil through prayer and the sacramentals.
know: Spelled 'Asmodaeus' in this translation.
Killed Sarah's seven husbands (Tob 3:8).
Fled to Egypt and was bound by Raphael (Tob 8:3).

name: Eldad
summary: One of the seventy elders chosen to share Moses' burden. Though he stayed in the camp rather than going to the Tent of Meeting, the Spirit rested on him and he prophesied; when Joshua asked Moses to stop him, Moses replied, 'I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets.'
catholic: The episode (read on the 26th Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year B, with Mk 9:38-48) is used to teach that the Spirit is not confined by human boundaries, and Moses' wish that all God's people be prophets is seen as fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2:17-18) and in the prophetic office shared by all the baptized.
know: One of the seventy elders (Num 11:26).
Prophesied in the camp with Medad.
Moses refused to forbid him (Num 11:29).

name: Eleazar the scribe
summary: One of the principal scribes, a man of ninety, who under Antiochus IV refused to eat swine's flesh and even refused the friendly offer to pretend to eat it, lest he lead the young astray. He went willingly to the rack, declaring that he suffered gladly 'because of my fear of him', leaving his death 'an example of nobleness'.
catholic: 1 and 2 Maccabees are deuterocanonical books, received in the Church's canon (Rome 382, Hippo 393, Carthage 397, Florence, and defined at Trent in 1546) though not in the Hebrew Bible or Protestant Old Testament. Eleazar is a model of integrity: he refuses even a pretended apostasy that would scandalize others (2 Macc 6:24-28), anticipating Christian teaching on scandal and martyrdom. The Fathers (e.g. St Gregory Nazianzen's oration on the Maccabees) honored him among the martyrs of the Old Covenant; the Eastern Churches commemorate him with the Maccabean martyrs on August 1, and Heb 11:35 is often read as alluding to these martyrs.
know: Ninety years old (2 Macc 6:24).
Refused to pretend to eat pork (2 Macc 6:21-28).
'Leaving his death for an example of nobleness' (2 Macc 6:31).

name: Epaphroditus
summary: Epaphroditus was sent by the Philippian church to bring their gift to the imprisoned Paul and to serve him. He fell sick nearly to death 'for the work of Christ', recovered, and was sent home with the Letter to the Philippians.
catholic: Paul calls him 'your apostle' (Greek apostolos, 'envoy') and asks that such people be held in honor (Phil 2:29).
know: 'My brother, fellow worker, fellow soldier' (Phil 2:25).
Nearly died serving Paul (Phil 2:27-30).
Brought the Philippians' gift (Phil 4:18).

name: Gamaliel
role: Pharisee and teacher of the Law
summary: Gamaliel was a Pharisee and teacher of the Law honored by all the people. When the Sanhedrin wanted to kill the apostles, he counselled restraint: if this movement is of men it will fail, but if it is of God they cannot overthrow it. Paul later says he was educated 'at the feet of Gamaliel'.
catholic: Gamaliel's counsel (Acts 5:38-39) is often cited as a model of prudent openness to the work of God. Tradition holds that he later became a Christian, and his relics were reported found in 415 together with those of St Stephen.
know: A respected Pharisee and member of the council.
Advised the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone (Acts 5:38-39).
Paul's teacher in the Law (Acts 22:3).
Tradition (not Scripture) holds he became a Christian.

name: Huldah
summary: Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum keeper of the wardrobe, lived in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem. When Josiah's officials brought her the newly found book of the law, she confirmed God's coming judgement on Judah but promised that Josiah, because his heart was tender, would die in peace before it.
catholic: Huldah is one of the few women named as prophets in the Old Testament (with Miriam and Deborah); Josiah's officials sought God's word through her, showing that prophetic charism is given to women as well as men - a gift the Church recognises in the Virgin Mary and in women saints and Doctors of the Church.
know: Prophetess consulted by Josiah's officials
Authenticated the book of the law
Foretold judgement and Josiah's peaceful death

name: Hymenaeus
summary: Hymenaeus made shipwreck of the faith; Paul 'delivered him to Satan' with Alexander so that they might learn not to blaspheme. With Philetus he taught that the resurrection had already taken place, upsetting the faith of some.
catholic: His case illustrates the Church's discipline: exclusion from communion meant to be medicinal ('that they might be taught'), and the duty of pastors to guard sound doctrine, including the bodily resurrection to come.
know: Handed over to Satan by Paul (1 Tim 1:20).
Taught that the resurrection was already past (2 Tim 2:17-18).

name: Jabez
summary: Jabez, 'more honourable than his brothers', was named in sorrow by his mother but prayed that God would bless him, enlarge his border and keep him from harm, 'and God granted him that which he requested'.
catholic: The short prayer of Jabez is a reminder within the genealogies that God hears personal, confident petition.
know: His prayer is recorded in the middle of a genealogy

name: Jacob
summary: Jacob son of Matthan is named in Matthew's genealogy as the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born (Mt 1:15-16).
catholic: Matthew arranges these generations into three sets of fourteen (Mt 1:17), presenting Jesus as the heir of Abraham and of David's royal house through his legal father Joseph.
know: Father of St Joseph according to Matthew 1:16.
Luke 3:23 instead reads Joseph 'son of Heli'; Julius Africanus (3rd c.) explained the two by a levirate marriage, others take Luke's line as Mary's.
Grandfather (legally) of Jesus.

name: Jairus
summary: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, begged Jesus to come to his dying twelve-year-old daughter. While Jesus was delayed healing a woman with a flow of blood, word came that the girl had died; Jesus said, 'Don't be afraid, only believe', took her by the hand - 'Talitha cumi' - and raised her.
catholic: The raising of Jairus's daughter is one of the Gospel signs restoring the dead to earthly life that point to Christ's own, greater Resurrection (CCC 646). Jesus took only Peter, James and John with the parents, a sign of the inner circle.
know: A ruler of the synagogue (Mk 5:22).
'Don't be afraid, only believe' (Mk 5:36).
His daughter, aged twelve, was raised from the dead (Mk 5:41-42).

name: Jehosheba
summary: Jehosheba (Jehoshabeath), daughter of King Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah and wife of the priest Jehoiada, rescued her infant nephew Joash from Athaliah's massacre and hid him in the Temple for six years.
catholic: By saving the last heir of David, Jehosheba preserved the line from which the Messiah would come; she is often compared to the women who protected Moses and to the Holy Family's flight from Herod's massacre.
know: Saved the infant Joash
Wife of Jehoiada the priest
Hid Joash in the Temple six years

name: Joanna
summary: Joanna, wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, was healed by Jesus and with other women supported him and the Twelve from her means. She was among the women who found the tomb empty and told the apostles.
catholic: Joanna shows the Gospel reaching even Herod's court. She is honoured among the myrrh-bearing women, the first heralds of the Resurrection.
know: Wife of Chuza, Herod's steward (Lk 8:3).
Provided for Jesus and the Twelve from her possessions.
Witness of the empty tomb (Lk 24:10).

name: Jochebed
summary: Levite woman, daughter of Levi and wife of Amram, mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. When Pharaoh ordered Hebrew boys drowned, she hid the infant Moses for three months, then set him in a papyrus basket on the Nile - and was hired by Pharaoh's daughter to nurse her own son.
catholic: Jochebed is a model of courageous motherhood defending a child's life against a death-decree, a scene the Fathers compared with the Holy Family's flight from Herod. The ark-basket (the same Hebrew word as Noah's ark) in which she placed Moses has been read as a figure of salvation through water, and her faith is praised in Hebrews 11:23.
know: Daughter of Levi; wife of Amram (Num 26:59).
Hid Moses three months and placed him in a basket on the Nile (Exo 2:2-3).
Was paid to nurse her own son (Exo 2:9).
Mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

name: Joel
summary: Joel son of Pethuel saw a devastating plague of locusts as a sign of the coming Day of the LORD and called the people to fasting and wholehearted repentance. He promised that afterwards God would pour out his Spirit on all flesh — sons and daughters, old and young, servants and handmaids.
catholic: On Pentecost St Peter declared that Joel's prophecy of the outpouring of the Spirit was fulfilled (Acts 2:16-21); the Church sees in it the gift of the Spirit to the whole messianic people, communicated in Confirmation (CCC 1287). Joel 2:12-18 ('return to me with all your heart... rend your heart and not your garments') is the first reading of Ash Wednesday, opening Lent.
know: Son of Pethuel (Joel 1:1); date of ministry uncertain.
Locust plague as a call to repentance (Joel 1-2).
'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' (Joel 2:28) — quoted at Pentecost.
Read on Ash Wednesday.

name: Judas (Jude), 'brother of the Lord'
summary: Judas (Mark: 'Judah') is listed among the 'brothers' of Jesus by the people of Nazareth (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3).
catholic: The Church understands him as a kinsman of Jesus (CCC 500). Catholic tradition generally identifies him with Jude, 'brother of James', author of the Letter of Jude (Jude 1), and often also with the apostle Jude Thaddeus, though the identifications are traditional rather than certain.
know: Named among Jesus' 'brothers' (Mt 13:55).
Mark's Gospel gives the form 'Judah' (Mk 6:3).
Traditionally linked with the author of the Letter of Jude.

name: Lo-ruhamah
summary: Gomer's daughter, named Lo-ruhamah ('not pitied') as a sign that God would no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; God later promises, 'I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy'.
catholic: Her renaming from 'not pitied' to 'pitied' is applied in the New Testament to the Church: 'who once had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy' (1 Pet 2:10).
know: Name means 'not pitied / not loved'.
Hos 1:6 does not say she was born 'to him', which some read as a hint of Gomer's infidelity.
Reversed in Hos 2:23.

name: Lydia
summary: Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from Thyatira and a worshipper of God, heard Paul at a place of prayer by the river outside Philippi. The Lord opened her heart; she and her household were baptized, and she insisted that the missionaries stay in her house, which became the meeting place of the Philippian church.
catholic: Lydia is the first recorded convert in Europe and a model of hospitality and of a woman whose heart the Lord opens to the Word. The baptism of her whole household (Acts 16:15) is among the New Testament passages the Church points to in the tradition of baptizing entire families, including children.
know: A seller of purple from Thyatira.
First recorded convert in Europe (Philippi).
Baptized with her household (Acts 16:15).
Hosted Paul and Silas after their release from prison (Acts 16:40).

name: Matthias
summary: After the death of Judas Iscariot, Peter led the 120 disciples in choosing a replacement from among those who had accompanied Jesus from his baptism to his ascension. Two were put forward, Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias; after prayer they cast lots, and the lot fell on Matthias, who was numbered with the eleven apostles.
catholic: The election of Matthias is the first act of the Church after the Ascension and shows that the apostolic office ('his office let another take', Acts 1:20) continues after its holder: the root of the doctrine of apostolic succession (CCC 861-862). Peter takes the initiative, an early sign of his primacy among the Twelve. The restoration of the number twelve signifies the Church as the new Israel of twelve tribes. Feast May 14.
know: Chosen by lot after prayer to replace Judas Iscariot.
Had to be a witness of Jesus' ministry from John's baptism to the Ascension (Acts 1:21-22).
His election made the Twelve complete again before Pentecost.
Feast May 14.

name: Medad
summary: Elder of Israel who, with Eldad, received the Spirit and prophesied in the camp, prompting Moses' wish that all the LORD's people were prophets.
catholic: See Eldad: their story is read as an image of the Spirit's freedom and the prophetic dignity of all God's people.
know: Prophesied in the camp with Eldad (Num 11:26-27).
Joshua's jealousy for Moses was gently rebuked.

name: Micah
summary: Micah of Moresheth, a contemporary of Isaiah, prophesied under Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah against the injustice of Samaria and Jerusalem, foretelling that Zion would be ploughed like a field. He also announced a ruler from little Bethlehem Ephrathah and summed up true religion: 'to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God'.
catholic: The chief priests and scribes cited Micah 5:2 to Herod as the prophecy that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem (Mt 2:5-6); the Church reads 'she who is in labour gives birth' (Mic 5:3) of the Virgin Mary, and Mic 5 is read on the Fourth Sunday of Advent (Year C). The 'Reproaches' (Improperia) of the Good Friday liturgy — 'My people, what have I done to you?' — echo Micah 6:3.
know: From Moresheth in Judah; contemporary of Isaiah.
Bethlehem prophecy (Mic 5:2), quoted in Mt 2:6.
'Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly' (Mic 6:8).
His warning to Hezekiah was remembered at Jeremiah's trial (Jer 26:18-19).

name: Onesimus
summary: Onesimus was a slave of Philemon at Colossae who left his master and came to Paul in prison, where Paul became his father in the faith. Paul sent him back with the Letter to Philemon, asking Philemon to receive him 'no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother', and offering to repay anything he owed. Colossians calls him 'the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you'.
catholic: The Letter to Philemon shows how communion in Christ transforms social relations; the Catechism cites Paul's request that the Christian master treat his Christian slave 'no longer as a slave but... as a brother' in teaching that enslaving human beings is a sin against their dignity (CCC 2414). His name means 'useful', and Paul plays on it (Philem 11). An Onesimus was bishop of Ephesus in the time of St Ignatius of Antioch, and some identify him with this Onesimus; this is possible but not certain.
know: A slave of Philemon; his name means 'useful' (Philem 10-11).
Converted by Paul during Paul's imprisonment.
Sent back to Philemon as a 'beloved brother' (Philem 16).
Travelled with Tychicus to Colossae (Col 4:9).

name: Onesiphorus
summary: Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains; when he came to Rome he searched diligently until he found the imprisoned apostle, and he had served much at Ephesus. Paul prays mercy on his household and on him.
catholic: Paul prays that the Lord grant Onesiphorus mercy 'in that day' (2 Tim 1:18) while greeting only his household (2 Tim 4:19); many Catholic interpreters infer that he had died, making this a New Testament example of prayer for the dead (cf. CCC 1032). The text does not state that he had died.
know: Sought out and found Paul in prison at Rome (2 Tim 1:17).
Paul prays mercy for him 'in that day' (2 Tim 1:18).
Paul greets 'the house of Onesiphorus' (2 Tim 4:19).

name: Orpah
summary: Moabite widow of Chilion who set out with Naomi but, at Naomi's urging, kissed her and returned to her people and her gods.
catholic: Orpah's departure throws Ruth's fidelity into relief; spiritual writers contrast the two as the soul that turns back and the soul that clings to God.
know: Moabite wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10).
Kissed Naomi and turned back (Ruth 1:14-15).

name: Publius
summary: Publius, the chief man of Malta, received Paul and the shipwrecked company for three days. Paul prayed, laid his hands on Publius' father, who lay sick with fever and dysentery, and healed him; many others on the island were then healed.
catholic: Tradition holds that Publius became the first bishop of Malta. Paul's prayer with the laying on of hands for the sick connects with the Church's ministry of healing.
know: Chief man of Malta (Acts 28:7).
His father was healed by Paul (Acts 28:8).

name: Rufus
summary: Paul greets Rufus, 'the chosen in the Lord', and his mother, who had been a mother to Paul as well.
catholic: Many interpreters suggest he is the Rufus whom Mark names as a son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried Jesus' cross (Mark 15:21), but this cannot be proven.
know: 'Chosen in the Lord' (Rom 16:13).
His mother had been like a mother to Paul.
Possibly the son of Simon of Cyrene (Mark 15:21).

name: Simeon
role: Righteous man who received the Christ child
summary: Simeon, a righteous and devout man of Jerusalem awaiting the consolation of Israel, had been told by the Holy Spirit he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ. When Mary and Joseph presented Jesus in the Temple, he took the child in his arms, blessed God, and foretold that Jesus would be a sign spoken against and that a sword would pierce Mary's soul.
catholic: Simeon's canticle, the Nunc Dimittis ('Now, Lord, you let your servant go in peace', Lk 2:29-32), is prayed every night at Night Prayer (Compline). At the Presentation (February 2) he recognizes Jesus as 'a light for revelation to the Gentiles', which gives the feast its candle blessing (Candlemas). The Church sees in the Presentation Christ's first offering of himself (CCC 529), and his prophecy is the first of the Seven Sorrows of Mary.
know: Promised he would see the Christ before death (Lk 2:26).
Took the infant Jesus in his arms in the Temple (Lk 2:28).
Spoke the Nunc Dimittis (Lk 2:29-32).
Prophesied the sword that would pierce Mary's soul (Lk 2:35).

name: Simon, 'brother of the Lord'
summary: Simon is listed among the 'brothers' of Jesus by the people of Nazareth (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3).
catholic: As with James and Joses, the Church understands Simon as a kinsman of Jesus, not a son of Mary (CCC 500). Tradition (Hegesippus, in Eusebius) speaks of Symeon son of Clopas, a cousin of the Lord who became the second bishop of Jerusalem and was martyred under Trajan; many identify him with this Simon, though this is not certain.
know: One of four 'brothers' named at Nazareth (Mk 6:3).
Possibly the Symeon son of Clopas whom Tradition makes second bishop of Jerusalem.
Distinct from Simon Peter and Simon the Zealot in Scripture.

name: Theophilus
summary: Theophilus is the 'most excellent' person to whom Luke dedicates his Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles, so that he may know the certainty of what he has been taught.
catholic: His title suggests a person of rank, perhaps Luke's patron. Since the name means 'friend of God', the Fathers (e.g. St Ambrose) also read it as addressing every reader who loves God.
know: Addressed in Luke 1:3 and Acts 1:1.
His name means 'friend of God'.
Addressee of Luke 1:3 and Acts 1:1.
Name means 'friend of God' or 'loved by God'.
Called 'most excellent', a title of rank.

name: Abiud
summary: Abiud, son of Zerubbabel, appears only in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus as the father of Eliakim (Mt 1:13), in the line of David's royal heirs after the Babylonian exile.
catholic: Matthew arranges these generations into three sets of fourteen (Mt 1:17), presenting Jesus as the heir of Abraham and of David's royal house through his legal father Joseph.
know: Named only in Matthew 1 - a link in Jesus' royal Davidic line after the exile.
Son of Zerubbabel; father of Eliakim.

name: Agur son of Jakeh
summary: The otherwise unknown sage to whom Proverbs 30 is attributed, who confesses his ignorance of the Holy One and asks God for 'neither poverty nor riches'.
catholic: Agur's question 'What is his name, and what is his son's name?' (Prov 30:4) has long been read by Christians as a veiled pointer to the Son of God. His prayer for 'neither poverty nor riches' (Prov 30:8-9) is a classic of Christian teaching on detachment and daily bread.
know: Author of Proverbs 30.
Era unknown; placed here with the wisdom tradition.

name: Andronicus
summary: Andronicus, with Junia, was a relative and fellow prisoner of Paul, 'notable among the apostles', who had come to Christ before Paul.
catholic: With Junia he is honored as a saint; they are commonly regarded as a missionary couple. 'Apostles' here is generally understood in the wider sense of missionaries sent by the churches, distinct from the Twelve.
know: Greeted with Junia in Rom 16:7.
A believer before Paul's conversion.
Shared imprisonment with Paul.
Murdered Onias (2 Macc 4:34).
Executed by Antiochus (2 Macc 4:38).

name: Anna
summary: Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, was a widow of great age who never left the Temple, worshipping with fasting and prayer night and day. Coming up at the Presentation, she gave thanks to God and spoke of the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
catholic: With Simeon, Anna represents faithful Israel waiting for the Messiah and welcoming him at the Presentation (CCC 529). Her life of prayer and fasting in the Temple makes her a patroness of widows and of consecrated life.
know: Daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (Lk 2:36).
A widow who served God in the Temple night and day (Lk 2:37).
Spoke of Jesus to all awaiting Jerusalem's redemption (Lk 2:38).

name: Antipas
summary: Antipas is called by the risen Christ 'my witness, my faithful one, who was killed among you' in the letter to the church at Pergamum, 'where Satan's throne is'.
catholic: He is honored as a martyr; tradition holds that he was bishop of Pergamum. Christ's own title 'faithful witness' (Rev 1:5) is given to him, showing the martyr's share in Christ's witness.
know: Martyred at Pergamum (Rev 2:13).
Called 'my faithful witness' by Christ.

name: Archelaus
summary: Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, ruled Judea, Samaria and Idumea after his father's death (4 BC - AD 6) until Rome deposed him for misrule. Fearing him, Joseph withdrew with the child and Mary to Galilee and settled in Nazareth.
catholic: Many commentators see an echo of his journey to Rome to receive his kingdom, and the delegation sent against him, in Jesus' parable of the nobleman (Lk 19:12-14).
know: Son of Herod the Great (Mt 2:22).
His reign is why the Holy Family settled in Nazareth (Mt 2:22-23).
Deposed by Augustus in AD 6.

name: Bartimaeus
summary: Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, was a blind beggar at Jericho. Hearing that Jesus was passing, he cried out, 'Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!' and would not be silenced; throwing off his cloak he came to Jesus, received his sight, and followed him on the way.
catholic: His persistent cry joins the Gospel prayers of mercy that shaped the 'Jesus Prayer' and the Kyrie eleison. He confesses Jesus by the messianic title 'Son of David', and his following 'on the way' to Jerusalem makes him a model disciple.
know: Son of Timaeus (Mk 10:46).
Called Jesus 'Son of David' (Mk 10:47).
Healed at Jericho and followed Jesus (Mk 10:52).

name: Caesar Augustus
summary: Augustus, the first Roman emperor (27 BC - AD 14), issued the decree that 'all the world should be enrolled', which brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, the city of David, where Jesus was born.
catholic: Luke sets the birth of the Prince of Peace in the reign of the emperor hailed as bringer of the Pax Romana and 'saviour', quietly contrasting the two. The Fathers saw God's providence using the census to fulfil the prophecy that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem (Mic 5:2).
know: First Roman emperor.
His census decree brought the Holy Family to Bethlehem (Lk 2:1-4).
Reigned when Jesus was born.

name: Clement
summary: Clement is named by Paul among his fellow workers at Philippi, 'whose names are in the book of life'.
catholic: Some early writers (e.g. Origen and Eusebius) identified him with St Clement of Rome, the third successor of Peter and author of the Letter to the Corinthians; this identification is uncertain.
know: Named as Paul's fellow worker (Phil 4:3).

name: Cleopas
role: Disciple on the road to Emmaus
summary: On the evening of the Resurrection, Cleopas and a companion walked to Emmaus. The risen Jesus joined them unrecognized, opened the Scriptures about himself, and was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
catholic: The Emmaus account is a pattern of the Mass: the Liturgy of the Word, in which Christ explains the Scriptures, followed by the Liturgy of the Eucharist, in which he takes, blesses and breaks the bread (CCC 1347). 'Stay with us, for it is nearly evening' inspired St John Paul II's letter Mane Nobiscum Domine for the Year of the Eucharist.
know: One of two disciples on the road to Emmaus (Lk 24:13-18).
Recognized Jesus 'in the breaking of the bread' (Lk 24:35).
Sometimes identified with Clopas (Jn 19:25), but this is uncertain.

name: Clopas
summary: Clopas is known only as the husband of Mary who stood by the cross of Jesus (Jn 19:25).
catholic: Tradition (Hegesippus, preserved by Eusebius) says Clopas was the brother of St Joseph and the father of Symeon, second bishop of Jerusalem. Some ancient writers identified him with Cleopas of Emmaus or with Alphaeus, but these identifications are uncertain.
know: Named once in Scripture (Jn 19:25).
By Tradition, brother of St Joseph.
By Tradition, father of Symeon, second bishop of Jerusalem.

name: Daughters of Philip (four)
summary: Philip the evangelist had four virgin daughters who prophesied; Paul and his companions stayed in their house at Caesarea.
catholic: They witness to the charism of prophecy given to women in the apostolic Church, fulfilling Joel's word quoted at Pentecost ('your daughters will prophesy', Acts 2:17).
know: A group of four unmarried sisters.
Exercised the gift of prophecy (Acts 21:9).

name: Dionysius the Areopagite
summary: Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus council of Athens, was one of the few who believed after Paul's speech on the 'unknown god'.
catholic: Early tradition (Dionysius of Corinth, via Eusebius) names him the first bishop of Athens. Influential mystical writings of about AD 500 were later circulated under his name ('Pseudo-Dionysius'), and in the West he was long confused with St Denis of Paris.
know: A member of the Areopagus (Acts 17:34).
Converted by Paul's Areopagus speech.
Writings attributed to him are by a later author ('Pseudo-Dionysius').

name: Diotrephes
summary: Diotrephes, 'who loves to be first', refused to acknowledge the Elder's authority, spread malicious words, would not welcome the travelling brothers, and expelled from the church those who did.
catholic: He is the New Testament's portrait of ambition and rejection of apostolic authority within the Church.
know: 'Loves to be first among them' (3 John 9).
Refused hospitality to the brothers and expelled those who gave it (3 John 10).

name: Dositheus (bearer of the Purim letter)
